S10_1_5_2_2_001_valid__exact_arithmetic_.rationale: batch119: independent fresh-context FIXTURE review against pinned J3/24-007 sections 10.1.5.2.2 and 10.1.5.3.1 and Table 10.4, plus integrator reproduction. These two subclauses were singled out by the batch101 review as the part of the numeric and character operation material that is genuinely portable: everything around them is hedged, because 7.4.3 makes real and complex values approximations and 10.1.5.2.4 permits the processor to evaluate any mathematically equivalent alternative, but integer division and character concatenation are exact. Integer division requires the result to be the integer closest to the mathematical quotient and between zero and the quotient inclusively, which is truncation toward zero; concatenation appends the right operand to the left and its length is the sum of the operand lengths. Non-vacuity was established by MUTATION rather than inspection, per the batch118 precedent. The reviewer applied and reported: 28 numeric expected literals perturbed by one, all failing; 9 character expected literals altered at equal length, all failing; 3 kind-expression expectations perturbed, all failing; 13 completion-token literals altered, all failing the suite stdout expectation; an operand-order swap in a concatenation fixture, failing; and a LEN assertion changed from 5 to 4, failing. Every hand oracle was independently recomputed from the source with no differences found. On the decisive question for integer division, whether the fixtures distinguish the standard's truncation toward zero from the common wrong implementation of flooring, the reviewer determined that 2 of the 4 integer-division fixtures discriminate, namely the negative-dividend case where minus eight divided by three is minus two under the standard and minus three under flooring, and the negative-divisor case; the other two use operands where truncation and flooring agree and therefore establish the result type and the basic quotient rather than the truncation direction. That limitation is recorded rather than glossed. One further limitation is recorded explicitly: appending a trailing blank to an expected character literal survived as a mutation for all 9 character value assertions, because character comparison blank-pads the shorter operand. The design nevertheless holds, because each value comparison is paired with an explicit LEN assertion and with test-module content pins, so a wrong length is caught even though the value comparison alone would not catch it; the reviewer judged this non-blocking on that basis. No fixture computes an expected value with MOD, MODULO, FLOOR, CEILING, INT or NINT for division, or with TRIM, INDEX, REPEAT or LEN_TRIM for concatenation; expected values are hand-computed literal constants. No oracle is built over real or complex values. Table 10.4 was verified row by row from the table itself because extraction interleaves columns, confirming the concatenation operator, its name, the x1 // x2 form and the operation description. Two facets were deliberately left pending, nondefault-same-kind-profile and different-kind-boundary, because nondefault character kinds are processor dependent and a mixed-kind concatenation is a diagnostic boundary rather than a portable runtime effect; the reviewer confirmed both deferrals are justified and that no testable facet was silently dropped. The generator --check mode reproduces byte-identical output. The integrator independently reproduced both compiler runs: all 13 cases pass under the frozen LFortran 0.65.0-411-ga0afaa840b-dirty, and all 13 pass under gfortran 16.1.0 with -std=f2023, which reports agreement on 13 of 13 cases. gfortran f2023 is the qualifying reference; compiler consensus is not itself an oracle, and the hand arithmetic was verified independently of both compilers. No LFortran gap was observed and tests/expected_failures.txt is unchanged. Decision: eligible with non-blocking observations.

S10_1_5_4_1_001_valid__logical_intrinsic.rationale: Independent fresh-context fixture review: doc/source_audits/batch_134.json. Accepted with no findings. THIS IS THE MATERIAL THAT BLOCKED BATCH127, where logical truth tables were VACUOUS because .AND. was asserted only on rows where .EQV. behaves identically, so substituting the wrong operator left the tests PASSING under both compilers - a defect that survived a 114-mutation oracle/input/omission campaign, because when the operator is wrong the oracle is wrong with it. The reviewer therefore re-ran ALL TWELVE generated operator substitutions on both toolchains: 24/24 compiled then failed at runtime, 0 unexpected passes, including the three prior survivors AND-to-EQV at FF, EQV-to-AND at FF and OR-to-NEQV at TT. The truth tables match Table 10.6 and every binary operator asserts the full TT/TF/FT/FF set directly in the emitted sources, so each table is inconsistent with all three alternatives - .AND. and .EQV. separated only at FF, .OR. and .NEQV. only at TT. The substitutions are PERMANENT generator data (BINARY_TRUTH_TABLES, DISCRIMINATION_ROWS, add_operator_mutations), not a one-off check. The reviewer also audited the unusually dense 21-facets-from-6-cases binding facet by facet and found NO over-binding: result-type checks observe the EXPRESSION directly rather than a variable that would launder it, which is the defect that forced a facet withdrawal in batch125. No result-kind claim is made anywhere, respecting the 10.1.9.3 p4 precedent that only one of the operand kinds is required.

S10_2_3_2_001_valid__where_masking_const.rationale: batch120: independent fresh-context FIXTURE review against pinned J3/24-007 sections 10.2.3.1 and 10.2.3.2, plus integrator reproduction. The batch109 source review identified the highest-value family in this scope as the requirement that assignment to elements not selected by the mask must not occur, which is directly observable by preloading unselected elements with distinguishable sentinels. Twenty-two facets of 10.2.3.2 are established across S10.2.3.2-001, -004, -005, -006, -007, -008 and -012, covering top-level control and pending masks, masked ELSEWHERE, final ELSEWHERE, END WHERE restoration, nested constructs, nested statements, and selected and unselected element values. All 34 facets of 10.2.3.1 remain pending because they are syntax, source-control or diagnostic constraints rather than runtime effects, and 19 of 10.2.3.2 remain pending: the p2 and p7 snapshot and call-count facets cannot be established because a conforming program cannot count mask evaluations, the p9, p10 and p11 evaluation facets have no portable oracle, the p13 and p14 facets are permissions rather than required effects, and the p3 sequence and p13 stable-mask facets are runtime-possible but were reasonably deferred to focused packets. Non-vacuity was proved by mutation rather than inspection, per the batch118 precedent, and the reviewer reported each campaign: ignoring the mask entirely failed 22 of 22; inverting the mask failed 22 of 22; perturbing an expected element by one failed 22 of 22; making a masked ELSEWHERE use its own mask alone without conjoining the previous pending mask failed 6 of 6; treating a nested construct as a statement failed 5 of 5; treating a nested statement as a construct with respect to the pending mask failed 1 of 1; and suppressing END WHERE restoration failed 3 of 3. The construct-versus-statement discrimination is the subtlest thing in the subclause and is genuinely established rather than assumed. S11_1_3_2_001_valid__associate_construct.rationale: batch121: independent fresh-context FIXTURE review against pinned J3/24-007 sections 11.1.3.1, 11.1.3.2 and 11.1.3.3, plus integrator reproduction. These are the FIRST Clause 11 fixtures in the suite: Clause 11.1 is fully source-registered at 268 of 268 base units but had no executable tests at all, so this packet establishes the pattern. Ten facets are established across S11.1.3.2-001, -002 and -003 and S11.1.3.3-001 and -005, covering selector evaluation before the block, the associate name identifying the evaluated entity, definability through the associate name, character length type parameter, rank and shape, and the associating entity's lower and upper bounds. Non-vacuity was proved by MUTATION rather than inspection, per the batch118 precedent, and the reviewer reported each campaign. The central bounds claim is that the associating entity's bounds DIFFER from the selector's subscripts, so mutating the expected LBOUND and UBOUND values to the selector's subscript values was applied and failed as required; the reviewer independently recomputed the extents, confirming that base(-3:3:2) has extent 4 and associated bounds 1 to 4, that base(12:20:3) has extent 3 and associated bounds 1 to 3, that SHAPE of the rank-two strided section is 3 by 2, and that LEN of the character section is 6. Mutating the expected LEN from 6 to 9, the parent's length, failed as required, which is the specific guard against the blank-padding trap; every length assertion uses LEN explicitly and never a character comparison, because comparison blank-pads the shorter operand and could otherwise succeed for the wrong reason. Omitting the assignment through the associate name failed, and an over-broad neighbour write would be caught by the adjacent-element check. The selector-evaluation-timing fixtures were checked to confirm that a re-evaluating implementation would give the different values the author named, which is the heart of 11.1.3.2 p1. Scalar perturbations by one failed across the remaining fixtures. One mutation was applied deliberately in the opposite direction: weakening the outer scoping sentinel to a value written inside the construct caused the test to stop discriminating, which proves the sentinel choice of 707, distinct from every value written inside, is doing real work rather than being decorative. The inquiry intrinsics LBOUND, UBOUND, SHAPE, SIZE, LEN and KIND are used as oracles, which is legitimate here only because the standard requires the asserted values rather than them being merely typical, and each plan states that justification; the packet does not claim to be testing those intrinsics themselves. The classification of definable-selector-assignment-control as a positive control rather than a full effect was examined and confirmed correct, because its owning requirement is a restriction. Twenty-three facets remain pending and the reviewer judged each deferral explicit and honest rather than a silent drop: several need polymorphic or SELECT TYPE context, branch-statement ownership for the END ASSOCIATE facets, coarray or CHANGE TEAM context, or unregistered Clause 15 attribute owners and Clause 19 scope isolation, and the kind facet was deferred rather than assume a non-default kind exists. No fixture assumes a non-default kind and no oracle is built over real or complex values. The generator --check mode reproduces byte-identical output. The integrator independently reproduced both compiler runs: all 10 cases pass under the frozen LFortran 0.65.0-411-ga0afaa840b-dirty and all 10 under gfortran 16.1.0 with -std=f2023, which reports agreement on 10 of 10 cases. gfortran f2023 is the qualifying reference; compiler consensus is not itself an oracle, and ASSOCIATE with strided array-section selectors is exactly where a compiler may be wrong, so the independently recomputed bounds and not the agreement are what validate these. No LFortran gap was observed and tests/expected_failures.txt is unchanged by this packet. Decision: eligible with non-blocking observations.

S9_7_1_2_001_valid__allocate_execution_b.rationale: Independent fresh-context fixture review: doc/source_audits/batch_128.json. Accepted with no blocking findings. The reviewer verified the PDF checksum and derived the ALLOCATE bounds rules itself: 9.7.1.2 p7 requires the array to be allocated with the SHAPE of source-expr and each lower bound equal to the corresponding element of LBOUND(source-expr), so SOURCE=s with s(-3:-1,5:8) correctly yields LBOUND [-3,5] rather than unit lower bounds - the claim most likely to be backwards. It confirmed bound-capture semantics (later redefinition of lo/hi does not affect allocated bounds), zero-extent allocation (upper<lower gives SIZE 0 while ALLOCATED is true per 9.7.1.3 p1, with no element read), and that the MOLD= fixture NEVER reads the undefined value, only fresh writes. Non-vacuity: the reviewer re-ran ALL 273 generated mutations, 273/273 killed, including all 11 feature-level ones; payload sentinels are nonzero, with zero appearing only for STAT=0, SIZE=0 and counters. No TRANSFER, LOC, ERRMSG, storage-layout, resource-exhaustion or undefined-value oracle is used. Every fixture asserts LBOUND and UBOUND, not merely SIZE, so a wrong-bounds allocator is rejected.

S9_7_3_2_001_valid__dealloc_allocated_co.rationale: Independent fresh-context fixture review with verified correction: doc/source_audits/batch_132.json. THE PRIMARY HAZARD IN THIS SECTION is that after deallocation an object's value is GONE and its contents are NOT observable - reading deallocated storage is undefined behaviour - and a pointer whose target was deallocated has UNDEFINED ASSOCIATION STATUS, so ASSOCIATED() on it is not a legitimate oracle. The reviewer checked all 11 emitted sources line by line and confirmed NO oracle reads deallocated storage, undefined association status, addresses, LOC, TRANSFER or ERRMSG content. The second structural requirement is that ALLOCATED(x)==.false. is a WEAK oracle on its own, because a processor that never allocated also reports false and .false. is default-equivalent; every fixture therefore establishes the POSITIVE state - ALLOCATED true plus bounds plus values - BEFORE deallocating, and the reviewer verified that before/after pairing in all 11. The packet was BLOCKED on finding C9732FR-001 because its fixtures were collected by run_tests.py but INVISIBLE to the unittest gate: there was no generator and no test module, so the cases could never regress and the mutation campaign was not reproducible from the committed tree. The correction added both; regeneration is byte-identical, the suite rose from 1016 to 1021, and the reviewer re-ran the feature-level mutations THROUGH THE GENERATOR - 12/12 failing as required, 11/11 reverse controls passing.
